name: Independent-Kinetic Screened Preferred-Frame
claimed_mechanism: A preferred-frame vector u^mu carries a lapse-weighted alpha coupling that is multiplied by e^-y, so the preferred-frame response is screened in high-density regions. The propagating scalar mode phi has its kinetic term normalized by an independent multiplier field N, not by the screened alpha, giving a finite mode kinetic normalization even when alpha is exponentially suppressed. The frozen mu(y)=1-e^{-y} enters only through the MOND interpolation, while matter remains minimally coupled to the single metric and G is not rescaled.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field, low-density limit y<<1, e^-y~1 and the preferred-frame alpha is unscreened, while mu(y)~y reproduces the MOND acceleration scale. In the high-density limit y>>1, alpha~e^-y is screened and the theory approaches GR, but the phi kinetic term remains finite because N is independent of alpha. The propagating mode therefore does not become singular or infinitely stiff as the preferred-frame response is screened, directly addressing the P7 collision.
inequivalence_argument: This architecture is inequivalent to every listed dead class because it changes the canonical field content and coupling topology: it adds an independent multiplier N that sources the finite propagating-mode kinetic normalization, whereas dead screened-preferred-frame classes tie the kinetic normalization to the same screened alpha or to a coefficient of the preferred-frame term. It is not a coefficient tweak, not a rescaling of G, not a second metric, and not a local renormalization of a killed architecture; the screened preferred-frame response and the finite mode kinetic are structurally decoupled.
